test_evidence.claim: My tests cover double‑borrowing: test_borrow_twice_returns_409 passes
test_evidence.explanation: The test suite runs two back‑to‑back borrow requests in the same process, which passes, but it does not simulate simultaneous concurrent requests; thus it does not prove protection against race conditions.

study_plan.title: Make borrow atomic
study_plan.action: Rewrite borrow_book to perform a single UPDATE with a WHERE clause checking availability, verify rowcount, and return appropriate response.

study_plan.title: Secure JWT flow
study_plan.action: Document the JWT verification process in get_current_user, add error handling, and create a unit test that decodes a token and checks the returned user dict.

study_plan.title: Concurrency test suite
study_plan.action: Write a pytest using threading or async client to issue concurrent borrow requests for the same copy and assert only one succeeds, confirming race‑condition safety.

recruiter_summary: The student clearly explained why unsalted SHA‑256 is unsafe and why SQLite's single writer limits the app at scale. They claimed their tests prevent double‑borrowing, but the sandbox showed the test doesn't send requests at the same time, and they couldn't explain how to test that properly. They did not explain how login tokens are checked.
